system:
You assess whether a hospital's own policies satisfy an accreditation requirement. You are shown the requirement and a numbered list of candidate policy provisions retrieved from the hospital's policy library.

Judge only what the provisions actually say. A provision that shares vocabulary with the requirement but addresses a different obligation does not satisfy it. A provision that satisfies the requirement in different words does satisfy it.

Answer NOT_COVERED only if none of the provisions addresses the requirement. Prefer PARTIAL when something related is present but incomplete: overstating a gap is worse than reporting one cautiously.
prompt:
REQUIREMENT [EM.16.01.01 EP 2]:
The hospital is required to conduct two exercises per year to test the emergency operations plan. 
- One of the annual exercises must consist of an operations-based exercise as follows: 
 - Full-scale, community-based exercise; or
 - Functional, facility-based exercise when a community-based exercise is not possible 
- The other annual exercise must consist of either an operations-based or discussion-based exercise as follows: 
 - Full-scale, community-based exercise; or
 - Functional, facility-based exercise; or
 - Mock disaster drill; or
 - Tabletop, seminar, or workshop that is led by a facilitator and includes a group discussion using narrated, clinically relevant emergency scenarios and a set of problem statements, directed messages, or prepared questions designed to challenge an emergency plan.
Exercises and actual emergency or disaster incidents are documented (after-action reports). 
Note 1: The hospital would be exempt from conducting its next annual operations-based exercise if it experiences an actual emergency or disaster incident (discussion-based exercises are excluded from exemption). An exemption only applies if the hospital provides documentation that it activated its emergency operations plan.
Note 2: See the Glossary for the definitions of operations-based and discussion-based exercises

**Attributes:** Documentation

**Crosswalk:** §482.15(d)(2)(i)(B), §482.15(d)(2)(i)(B), §482.15(d)(2)(i), §482.15(d)(2)(i), §482.15(d)(2)(ii)(B), §482.15(d)(2)(ii)(B), §482.15(d)(2)(ii)(C), §482.15(d)(2)(ii)(C), §482.15(d)(2)(i)(A), §482.15(d)(2)(i)(A), §482.15(d)(2), §482.15(d)(2), §482.15(d)(2)(ii)(A), §482.15(d)(2)(ii)(A)

CANDIDATE POLICY PROVISIONS:
[C1] Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §4 Training and Testing
Training and Testing
The program must be tested twice annually: at least one full-scale exercise and one additional exercise (which
may be tabletop). Exercises must involve community partners and external stakeholders when possible.

[C2] Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §5 After-Action Review
After-Action Review
Following each drill or actual emergency, an after-action review must be conducted, documented, and used to
update the EOP. Lessons learned must be incorporated within 90 days of the exercise.

[C3] Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §1 Risk Assessment & Planning
Risk Assessment & Planning
An all-hazards risk assessment must be conducted to identify likely emergency events (natural disasters, mass
casualty incidents, utility failures, cyber attacks, pandemics). The Emergency Operations Plan (EOP) must
address each identified risk.

[C4] Staffing and Delivery of Care §2 Acuity-Based Staffing
Acuity-Based Staffing
Patient assignments must be based on acuity and complexity of care needs, not just census. A validated patient
classification/acuity system should be used. High-acuity patients require more experienced nurses with lower
patient-to-nurse ratios.

[C5] Emergency Preparedness - Disaster Plan §2 Communications Plan
Communications Plan
An emergency communications plan must include: backup communications systems, procedures for notifying staff,
contact information for external agencies, patient tracking systems, and methods for communicating with
patients/families during emergencies.

[C6] Infection Control and Prevention §2 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Staff must select and use appropriate PPE based on transmission-based precautions. This includes gloves,
gowns, masks/respirators, and eye protection. PPE must be properly donned, doffed, and disposed of per
established protocol.

Reply with exactly these four lines and nothing else:
VERDICT: one of COVERED, PARTIAL, NOT_COVERED
EVIDENCE: candidate ids that support the verdict (e.g. C1, C3), or NONE
MISSING: what the requirement demands that no candidate provides, or NONE
REASON: one sentence citing what the provisions say
